global_organization_chain: Define health as five joint conditions, then build one score
Notice that rich countries dominate the ranking and test the hunch indicator by indicator
Read health against the curve income predicts, and pick the country furthest below it
Set the target as a percentage of a peer in the same income band, with the percentage varying by component
Reduce the indicators by a test, stage the policy, and admit the plan outruns reality

main_argument_chains.claim: Italy ranks mid-table in absolute health but last once income is accounted for, and a fifteen-year policy aimed at a discounted UK benchmark can carry it across the curve.
support_steps: Score 40 countries with combined weights and TOPSIS
Fit an exponential curve of the score on income
Find Italy furthest below it, falling from 26th to 40th
Take the UK, inside a 0.03 income band, as the benchmark
Set the vision at 95 percent of the UK overall, lower for connect and equal for sustainability
Choose five levers by ANOVA and stage them over three five-year periods
Simulate the path and report that it reaches the vision while conceding change is hard
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Compete for funds, reform university governance, recruit internationally, build top-1000 universities, and grow the researcher stock, with permission to revise after each stage.

warnings.warning: The normalization, weighting and TOPSIS formulas are private-use glyphs. Reconstructed in standard form. The combination rule for the three weight sets is never stated.
The fitted exponential is announced but its coefficients are illegible. The rank change, the income band and the vision percentages were kept.
The system dynamics model is a flow chart with no rate equation. The spending move from 1.5 to 2 percent of GDP and the rising path were kept; the 2035 level was not.
